content: Rifampin significantly impacts the pharmacokinetics of various drugs by inducing or inhibiting specific hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2B6, and UGT enzymes, as well as affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Below are detailed interactions and clinical recommendations for co-administration: 1. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin reduces the efficacy of these agents by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 2. BCG Vaccine (Live): Rifampin decreases the vaccine's efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Bedaquiline: Rifampin reduces bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially compromising its therapeutic effect. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 4. Belumosudil: Rifampin decreases belumosudil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Increase the belumosudil dose to 200 mg twice daily if co-administration is necessary, and monitor closely. 5. Bendamustine: Rifampin reduces bendamustine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for changes in therapeutic efficacy. 6. Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Rifampin decreases the levels of benzhydrocodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor for withdrawal symptoms or reduced analgesic efficacy. 7. Berotralstat: Rifampin reduces berotralstat levels via P-glycoprotein induction. Monitor closely and adjust the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates as needed. 8. Bexagliflozin: Rifampin reduces bexagliflozin levels by inducing UGT1A9 metabolism. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for glycemic control. 9. Bictegravir: Rifampin significantly reduces bictegravir plasma concentrations by inducing CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 metabolism, leading to potential therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Bosutinib: Rifampin reduces bosutinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, decreasing its plasma concentration by approximately 85%. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 11. Buprenorphine (Various Forms): Rifampin reduces buprenorphine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the buprenorphine dose or consider alternative formulations that allow dose adjustments. Monitor for withdrawal symptoms or respiratory depression. 12. Bupropion: Rifampin reduces bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced therapeutic efficacy. 13. Buspirone: Rifampin reduces buspirone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative anxiolytics. 14. Cabotegravir: Rifampin reduces cabotegravir systemic exposure by inducing UGT1A1 and UGT1A9 metabolism, potentially leading to virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Cabozantinib: Rifampin reduces cabozantinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or increase the cabozantinib dose if necessary, with close monitoring. 16. Caffeine: Rifampin reduces caffeine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 17. Calcifediol/Calcitriol: Rifampin reduces the half-life of calcifediol and calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum calcium and vitamin D levels, and adjust therapy as needed. 18. Canagliflozin: Rifampin reduces canagliflozin levels by inducing metabolism. Consider alternative antihyperglycemic agents in patients with reduced renal function. 19. Cannabidiol: Rifampin reduces cannabidiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor for reduced efficacy. 20. Carbamazepine: Rifampin reduces carbamazepine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative anticonvulsants. 21. Cariprazine: Rifampin reduces cariprazine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for reduced efficacy. 22. Carvedilol: Rifampin reduces carvedilol levels by inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 23. Caspofungin: Rifampin reduces caspofungin levels by inducing metabolism. Use caution and monitor for antifungal efficacy. 24. Ceftobiprole: Ceftobiprole increases rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 25. Celecoxib: Rifampin reduces celecoxib levels by inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 26. Cenobamate: Rifampin reduces cenobamate levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust the dose of cenobamate or CYP2B6 substrates as needed. 27. Ceritinib: Rifampin reduces ceritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 28. Cevimeline: Rifampin reduces cevimeline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy. 29. Chloramphenicol: Rifampin reduces chloramphenicol levels by inducing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 30. Chlordiazepoxide: Rifampin reduces chlordiazepoxide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced anxiolytic effects. 31. Chloroquine: Rifampin reduces chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced antimalarial efficacy. 32. Cholic Acid: Rifampin increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Avoid inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) and monitor liver function tests. 33. Cilostazol: Rifampin reduces cilostazol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative antiplatelet agents. 34. Cimetidine: Rifampin reduces cimetidine levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 35. Cinacalcet: Rifampin reduces cinacalcet levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 36. Citalopram: Rifampin reduces citalopram levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced antidepressant efficacy. 37. Clarithromycin: Rifampin reduces clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced antimicrobial efficacy. 38. Clofazimine: Clofazimine reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting absorption. Monitor closely for changes in therapeutic efficacy. This list highlights the necessity of careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or avoidance of co-administration when rifampin is used with these drugs.
